label: verify-t6-flyingfish-alt

claims.claim: Strongest rival is thrust-supported taxiing; the lemma excludes it, so field distances can exceed the glide bound without any law being wrong.
claims.source_says: (ground effect, updraft and taxiing thrust are outside, which is why the field glide distances exceed the bound). Davenport 1994: free flight 'may be prolonged by further taxiing'. taxiing-thrust.json: status proposed, not formalised.
claims.note: Flight.lean, the registry entry and Davenport 1994 support the exclusion and the taxiing prolongation, but 'strongest rival' is a judgment, not stated by any source.

claims.claim: Davenport 2003 holds the accepted ballistic-leap route to flight is flawed and taxiing-in-half-beaks came first.
claims.source_says: These data indicate that the accepted model of evolution of flight in flying fishes (by extension of ballistic leaps) is flawed; it is proposed that evolution of lift-supported surface taxiing in half-beaks ... was an essential preliminary

claims.claim: Flying snake: 9.62 m drop, 14 glides, mean 10.14 m; with 2-D L/D 2.7 and kinetic height subtracted the bound is 12.21 m; no elimination on average, L/D not whole-animal, upper tail exceeds it.
claims.source_says: 9.62 m branch; 14 glide sequences; 10.14+/-2.69 m while reaching an airspeed of 10.0+/-0.9 m/s. Section max L/D 2.7. (9.62-100/19.62)*2.7 = 12.2125; mean+sd 12.83 exceeds it.
claims.note: Numbers and arithmetic reproduce; the 2-D versus whole-animal caveat is the agent's own correct reading.

claims.claim: No public raw trajectory dataset for any gliding animal was found; only the Alsomitra CFD set (CC BY 4.0) and the oversized bat set (CC0, 6.7 GB) are open.
claims.source_says: DataCite: Dryad set 6747705573 bytes, CC0; Cranfield set CC BY 4.0, no size. My snake/Chrysopelea dataset search returned only GBIF occurrence downloads.
claims.note: Licences and size are confirmed and my snake search found none, but 'only these are open' is a broad negative I could not fully verify.

overall: Three of four key claims check out against the sources. The fourth is partly supported: the dataset licences and sizes match, but a negative search result can't be fully confirmed. 'Strongest rival' is a judgment, though the sources behind it are accurate.
